proof: Assume for contradiction that f(x0)<0 for some x0 in [0,1/4].
Choose N with 2/N < -f(x0). Prefix completeness gives q in Q with chi_q(n)=lambda(n) for every n<=N.
The prefixes cancel in f_q(x0)-f(x0). Since |chi_q(n)-lambda(n)|<=2 and |sin(2*pi*n*x0)|<=1, |f_q(x0)-f(x0)| <= 2*sum_{n>N} 1/n^2 < 2/N.
Therefore f_q(x0) <= f(x0)+|f_q(x0)-f(x0)| < 0, contradicting the assumed positivity of every q in Q.
Thus f>=0 on [0,1/4]. Conrey Theorem 1 then implies RH.
residual: RH-ANA-004a: GOOD_PREFIX_COMPLETE_PRIME_SELECTION — under prescribed local Legendre conditions matching lambda through arbitrarily long N, establish existence of the same primes q with the global no-overshoot condition S_q(qx)<=h(q) for all x<=1/4, or find a weaker source-valid positivity certificate; generic magnitude/density evidence is insufficient without a sign-preserving gluing theorem.

source_bound_representation.interpretation: The character-side residual is a one-sided Cesaro-overshoot constraint relative to the class-number endpoint h(q), not merely a magnitude bound.

statement.claim: If Q is lambda-prefix-complete and f_q(x)>=0 for every q in Q and every x in [0,1/4], then f(x)>=0 on [0,1/4], hence the Riemann Hypothesis follows by Conrey Theorem 1.
definitions: lambda is the Liouville function and f(x)=sum_{n>=1} lambda(n) sin(2*pi*n*x)/n^2.
For a prime q≡3 (mod 8), chi_q(n)=(n/q) and f_q(x)=sum_{n>=1} chi_q(n) sin(2*pi*n*x)/n^2.
A set Q of such primes is lambda-prefix-complete if for every integer N>=1 there exists q in Q with chi_q(n)=lambda(n) for all 1<=n<=N.
statement.scope: A reduction of Conrey's all-q sufficient condition to any prefix-complete good subfamily. It does not prove that such a good subfamily exists and does not claim equivalence with RH.
